reasons: Rule mis-applied: § 11.3 is an abuse/AUP enforcement right (IBM investigating potential breaches of the Customer's content/acceptable-use warranties in 11.2(b)), not a usage/licence-compliance or metering audit of the kind AUDIT targets. Burdening a security/illegal-content investigation right with audit-style limits is directionally wrong; if the contract truly lacks a usage-audit clause, the correct output is a 'missing/no-issue' finding, not this graft.

Internal inconsistency created in the edited paragraph: p0137 expressly preserves IBM's ability to act 'in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law' with only best-efforts notice, but the inserted proviso imposes an absolute 30 days' prior written notice and a once-per-12-month cap on 'any investigation' with no emergency carve-out — the two sentences now contradict each other and the once-a-year cap would bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident.

Cost-shift trigger is inapposite: there is no payment/quantity measurement in § 11.3, so 'unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated' is inoperative boilerplate transplanted from a licence-audit context and will read as a drafting error to the counterparty.

The blanket bar on 'direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records' and the off-site-satisfaction right sit awkwardly in a hosting agreement where IBM operates the environment and § 11.3(a)/(b) contemplate restricting access to or removing Content; as drafted it arguably neuters the remedies the rationale claims were left untouched, and it conflicts with p0138's obligation to provide all relevant information on request.

Comment overstates the baseline ('unlimited and unannounced ... walk-away') given p0137's existing best-efforts notice obligation, so the justification offered to the counterparty is not fully accurate.
